title: Buying Property in Your Wife or Parents' Name to Save Tax? The Benami & Section 64 Trap
angle: Salaried Indians register flats in their wife's name for a 1-2% stamp duty discount, but Section 64 clubs all rental income back to the husband—and parents face Benami notices.
outline: The common tax hack: Registering an apartment in a homemaker wife's or retired mother's name to claim female buyer stamp duty concessions (1-2% lower in Delhi, Haryana, Punjab, Maharashtra).

Section 64(1)(iv) Clubbing Trap: If the husband pays for the property from his bank account without genuine financial consideration from the wife, 100% of rental income and capital gains are legally taxed in the husband's high tax bracket.

The Benami Prohibition Risk: Buying property in parents' or siblings' names where you pay but they hold title can trigger Benami law confiscation, a 25% fair-value fine, and up to 7 years imprisonment.
Legitimate exceptions: Properties purchased for a spouse or unmarried child out of known taxable salary are exempt from Benami, but clubbing still applies.
How to structure it legitimately: Formal gift deed (tax-exempt under Section 56(2)(x) for linear ascendants/descendants) or joint home loan co-ownership based on actual salary contributions.
